newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat in West Bank, says no progress in talks.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in West Bank, says no progress in talks.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Thursday that a week of fresh talks with Israel on a long overdue withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron had achieved nothing.
Arafat spoke to legislators in Ramallah during his first trip to the West Bank since fierce Israeli-Palestinian clashes last month killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers.
"Until yesterday night, the brothers returned from the meetings and they have not reached anything," Arafat told the Palestinian Legislative Council, referring to Israeli-PLO talks in Gaza.
"Thus, we must be fully prepared...to confront all possibilities," he said.
The talks were renewed this week after unprecendented gun battles in the West Bank and Gaza Strip posed the biggest threat yet to Israel-PLO peace moves since they were launched in 1993.
Israeli officials said in response to Arafat's remarks that the Jewish state was bargaining in good faith.

"So far in the talks I think there is a readiness to hear each side's point of view and we don't necessarily have to be in agreement on all points but a serious exchanges of the issues that concern each side is very important for the negotiating process," said Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel.
"We all prefer slightly longer peace negotiations to a drastically shortened peace," he told Reuters.

Palestinians have pressed hardline Israeli leader Banjamin Netanyahu to live up to an agreement negotiated by Israel's previous Labour government more than a year ago to pull troops out of parts of Hebron, a city holy to Moslems and Jews.

Netanyahu wants added measures to protect 400 Jewish settlers who live among 100,000 Arabs. Palestinians say Israeli demands amount to reopening the agreement for negotiations, which they are not willing to do.
One Palestinians negotiator said late on Wednesday that Israel appeared to be coming around on some points.
"Apparently, the Israelis have come to understand the agreement has to be adhered to and they are studying the agreement," Hassan Asfour told Reuters.
But chief negotiator Saeb Erekat said he was not sure whether Israel "got the message".
Netanyahu, who ousted Labour part leader Shimon Peres in elections last May has said security measures Israel was seeking were all "within the confines of the existing agreement".

But Palestininan officials and Israeli security sources say Israel is demanding concessions that contradict the peace deal including reducing the number of Palestinian police allowed to enter Hebron and arming them with pistols instead of rifles.
Arafat also met in Ramallah with representatives of 40 international donor countries, calling on them to help rescue a Palestinian economy ravaged by an Israeli closure on the West Bank and Gaza.
"I have to ask you for urgent help to save our very critical situation. It is a real tragedy," he told the representatives.
An Israeli-PLO subcommittee was set to meet at the border between Israel and the Gaza Strip later on Thursday to discuss economic issues.
Later on Thursday chief Israeli and Palestinian negotiators were to meet in Jerusalem to decide on a venue for more talks next week.
